# Notices

Video64 canonical bitmap masks and structural research: Copyright (c) 2026 Shael Riley. MIT; see LICENSE. The runtime contains only canonical indices 0–31, in order, including Void. Parent and selected-byte hashes are in assets/provenance.json.

ANSI Tube palettes, palette grading and quantization, and structural descriptors originate with Shael Riley, at commit ee08e6659bdb060f0689457ee32b22ff7b4dc664. They are included in Video32 at the author’s express direction, including his instruction to publish this repository publicly. That upstream repository currently supplies no license notice. The included MIT notice covers Video64 material and new project code; it does not change the licensing of the ANSI Tube repository itself. Both upstream checkouts remain unchanged.

Native Glyph has no counterpart for uncolored canonical masks. Its registry entry is visible but unavailable; it never silently overrides finite depth. MooBurst’s palette and tonal treatment are preserved. Its separate cow-image cameo and sound treatment are omitted because this visualizer draws only canonical masks and leaves incoming audio unmodified.

No SoundSpectrum artwork, presets, source code, or other assets are copied. WhiteCap informs only the requested ambition and breadth. The currently accessible official pages describe combinations and broad effect counts without identifying the original edition’s bundled authored configuration count; that historical count remains unverified. The required authored floor is therefore 256.

Implementation is agent-authored with Codex from Shael Riley’s brief. No raw music is stored or transmitted, and the extension has no remote dependencies, accounts, analytics, or browsing host permissions.

## Revision palettes and spatial data

The revision picker intentionally replaces redundant palette choices. It contains 20 newly authored themes, five distinctive original artwork color paths, and 12 original treatments, plus unavailable Native Glyph. Historical upstream tables remain unchanged for provenance and parity; this is not a claim that every historical palette is still selectable.

The polygon bank's OSM source subsets and derived point fabrics retain ODbL 1.0. Required attribution is provided in the viewer's source link, controls and linked credits page; source subsets and derived data are offered in the public repository. CC0 Kenney models, BSD Freedoom level data and public-domain USGS terrain retain their own notices. Full level authorship and BSD text are bundled.

The spherical-video bank's glyph image data, metadata and image-derived previews are CC BY-SA 4.0 adaptations of the UGC360 Dataset. Only original source families CC BY, CC BY-SA and CC0 were selected; NC and ND entries were excluded. Source links, available authors, source licence families, dates, frame hashes, the source CSV and the complete CC BY-SA text are retained. This is a selection from the dataset's documented rights metadata; it is not an independent current-page rights audit. The MIT code licence does not replace these data licences.

Video studies contain nine complete 360° source frames, reduced and matched to the exact masks, with RGB565 colour and an artistic slow loop. Every longitude and latitude is retained, with an opening-heading rotation. They are monoscopic spheres without reconstructed depth. Native VR180 material found during research required gated access and was not imported. No source-video audio is included.

See [SPATIAL-SOURCES.md](SPATIAL-SOURCES.md), the per-bank manifests and `space-credits.html` for per-source attribution, adaptations, hashes and precise limits. Rendering assets are local and no runtime account or network service is introduced.
